## Answer: no, the repo ships zero agent-facing context

`crimes scan --format json` flags it directly — **`crime_00016` · Missing Agent Context** (`missing_agent_context`, universal pack), severity **medium**, confidence **0.9**, agent_risk **0.42**, effort **small**:

```
no AGENTS.md found at repo root
no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

All four discovery surfaces are empty. (The finding is anchored to `assets/cjs_shims.js` only because repo-level findings need a file to hang off — it's about the repo root, not that file.)

## What that costs you on this specific repo

The rest of the scan is the argument for why this one matters here. Three concrete failure modes an AGENTS.md would prevent:

**1. No command discovery.** The package ships two binaries (`tsup`, `tsup-node`) and 52 files, and nothing tells an agent how to build, test, or typecheck. First move on any PR is a guess.

**2. False green on verification.** There are **12 tests with zero `expect`/`assert` calls** (`crime_00052`–`crime_00063`, e.g. `"custom tsconfig"`, `"removeNodeProtocol works on shims"`) and **14 more** that only use weak matchers. An agent that runs the suite, sees green, and reports "verified" is wrong a meaningful fraction of the time. That's exactly the kind of thing a `## Testing` section has to warn about, because the test suite itself won't.

**3. Load-bearing files look ordinary.** `src/utils.ts` has **18 importers** and is 425 lines; `src/plugin.ts` has 10; `src/log.ts` has 9; `src/index.ts` fans out to 17 modules and holds a 293-line `build()`. Nothing in the tree signals "additive edits only" — an agent will refactor `utils.ts` on its first PR because it looks like a junk-drawer helper file, which it is, and which is also why 18 modules depend on it.

Net: the detector rates this at agent_risk 0.42 with **effort: small** — it's the cheapest high-leverage fix in the whole report. One file clears it.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector wants a root `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`, or a `SKILL.md` under `.claude/skills/`/`.agents/skills/`). Root `AGENTS.md` is the right pick — it's the cross-tool convention and needs no directory scaffolding.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Build tool for TypeScript libraries. Bundles with esbuild, emits types via
rollup-plugin-dts / api-extractor. Ships two binaries: `tsup`, `tsup-node`.

## Commands

- Install: `pnpm install`
- Build: `pnpm build`
- Test: `pnpm test`            # vitest, specs in `test/*.test.ts`
- Single test: `pnpm test -t "<test name>"`
- Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck`
- Lint: `pnpm lint`

## Layout

- `src/index.ts`        — public API + `build()` orchestrator (entry point)
- `src/esbuild/`        — esbuild runner and plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts`, `src/tsc.ts` — .d.ts generation paths
- `src/plugin.ts`       — plugin container/lifecycle
- `src/utils.ts`, `src/log.ts` — shared helpers
- `test/`               — integration tests; `test/utils.ts` is the shared harness

## Load-bearing files — prefer additive changes

Do not restructure these without reading their importers first:

- `src/utils.ts`  — 18 importers
- `src/plugin.ts` — 10 importers
- `src/log.ts`    — 9 importers
- `test/utils.ts` — 9 importers (changing the harness breaks most of the suite)

## Conventions

- Options flow through a single normalized `options` bag (`normalizeOptions`
  in `src/index.ts`). Add new options there, not at call sites.
- Plugins follow the esbuild plugin shape: `{ name, setup(build) }`.
- Errors surface through `src/log.ts` — don't `console.log` directly.

## Testing notes

- Tests are integration-level: they invoke a real build into a temp dir and
  assert on emitted output via `test/utils.ts`.
- **A green suite is weaker evidence than it looks.** Several tests assert
  nothing at all, and others only check that a build didn't throw. If you
  change behaviour, add an assertion on the emitted output — don't rely on
  an existing test to catch a regression.

## Safety

- Never edit `dist/` or `assets/` build artifacts by hand.
- Don't add new `*Sync` fs calls in `src/` — the codebase is migrating off them.
```

That's the whole fix. Re-running `crimes scan` after adding it should drop `crime_00016` and take the medium count from 38 to 37.

Two things I'd flag as assumptions in the skeleton above, since the scan doesn't carry them: the exact **script names** (`pnpm build` / `pnpm test` / `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint`) and the **package manager**. Read `package.json` `scripts` and confirm the lockfile before committing — wrong commands in an AGENTS.md are worse than no AGENTS.md, because agents will trust them. Everything else — layout, importer counts, the test-suite warning — comes straight out of the scan.
